svg.title: FlowSOM learning, metaclustering and cell assignment
svg.desc: Four connected stages show a hypothetical three-marker example. Selected cell measurements are centred by full-population marker medians, divided by their interquartile ranges with a unit fallback and multiplied by feature weights. One prepared cell has vector (0.2, 1.1, 0.4). Its Euclidean best-matching profile is number 6 on the four-by-four SOM grid. The highlighted square contains the winner and all eight neighbours at Chebyshev grid distance at most one, including diagonals. Every included profile moves towards the cell using the same learning rate. The example rate 0.2 changes the winning vector from (0.4, 0.8, 0.2) to (0.36, 0.86, 0.24). Further cell draws use a decreasing learning rate and grid radius. After training, average-linkage agglomeration groups the sixteen retained illustrative profile vectors into three metaclusters. Branch heights are the computed average Euclidean profile distances; node borders, branch colours and leaf strips encode the same metacluster mapping. Bars from left to right always mean markers M1, M2 and M3, with height proportional to the prepared value on a common zero-to-1.4 scale. A different cell j with vector (0.28, 0.22, 1.08) is closest to profile 12, at distance 0.115, and inherits its metacluster 3. Grid positions represent SOM neighbourhoods, not tissue coordinates. Values and cells are illustrative, not tissue results.
svg.text: B Match the cell, then update the grid neighbourhood
Repeat cell draws; decrease αₜ and rₜ
C Group the learned profile vectors
over all u in A and v in B
D Each cell inherits its closest profile’s metacluster
